decisions.statement: A row is built from the state a stream ended in.
A row is stamped with the millisecond the stream ended at.
The elapsed span is the end millisecond less the start millisecond.
The last frame's age is the end millisecond less the last frame's millisecond.
An `Error` is split into its constructor's name and its message.
Anything thrown that is no `Error` is split into its typeof and its string.
A stream that ended with nothing thrown carries a null error class.
A stream that ended with nothing thrown carries a null error message.
A held span the state leaves out is written as null rather than left out.
An empty pool reason the state leaves out is written as null.
The last `event:` line a chunk has names that chunk's event type.
A chunk with no `event:` line leaves the event type as that type was.
An `event:` line naming nothing sets the event type to the empty string.
A chunk is decoded once for both the event type and the stop.
One decoder serves every chunk this process has.
A chunk of no bytes is read no further.
An `event: message_stop` line anywhere in a chunk sets the stop.
A stream terminates once.
The first termination is the termination written down.
Arming a terminal callback after the termination runs that callback at once.
A stream that terminates leaves the shutdown flush before the row is built.
A shutdown flush ends every stream still entered.
A shutdown flush leaves the set with nothing.
The clock a shutdown flush stamps by is handed in so a test needs no real time.
The file a row lands beside is handed in rather than looked up.
A row is written through `page-entry-queue`.
A row handed over after a refusal is written rather than dropped.
Writing a row answers the refusal last met or null.
A row is written only where the caller handed a file in.
Anything thrown while a row is written is answered as a refusal.
`transportLogFlushed` resolves once every row handed over is on the disk.
A caller hands in the path of a page file that is already there.
A caller going down waits on `transportLogFlushed` before that caller goes down.
Nothing here reads the index.
Nothing here reads a seat's name.
Nothing here makes the page a row lands beside.
Nothing here reads a clock of its own.
Nothing here waits on the disk while a row is handed over.
Nothing here judges a row against the shape declaring that row.
A file that is not there is opened again for every row until that file is there.
A refusal is answered to the caller rather than kept.
A row not waited on reaches no file where the process goes down first.
A queue opened for a file is held for the life of the process.
A file this module opens beside a page reaches the listing at the next settle over that page.
No repository root reaches this module, so no index is named from here.
Nothing here has a lock against another writer of the same file.
An `event:` line divided across two chunks is read in neither chunk.
A chunk opening partway through a line is read as opening a line.
A shutdown flush stamps every row that flush ends with the one millisecond.

definition: what a gateway writes down about a stream once that stream has ended
